http://www.euronews.com/2026/08/03/myanm.text: Myanmar's detained former leader Aung San Suu Kyi met with the nation's Red Cross representative on Monday, the president's office said, the first publicised meeting between her and a foreign official since she was ousted in a 2021 military coup.The military deposed Suu Kyi in February 2021, jailing the Nobel Peace Prize laureate and triggering an ongoing civil war that has killed more than 100,000 people on all sides.The coup leader and former junta chief, Min Aung Hlaing, was installed as civilian president in April following highly restricted elections.Later that month, Suu Kyi, now 81, was moved to house arrest after Min Aung Hlaing said he had commuted the rest of her sentence.She was detained on a host of charges which rights groups say were concocted to sideline her and her popular National League for Democracy party.The president's office said in a statement that Arnaud de Baecque, the Resident Representative of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) to Myanmar, met with Suu Kyi on Monday morning.In photos released by the president's office, Suu Kyi is seen shaking hands with a man who appears to be de Baecque.Another image shows Suu Kyi cutting a birthday cake, and yet another shows the cake with text reading: "Happy Birthday Aunty Suu."The images could not be immediately verified by the AFP news agency but AI tools found no instances of fabrication."We are happy to see her photo like this if it's really her meeting with the ICRC. We can know now that she's alive," a veteran politician of her party told AFP on condition of anonymity."However, Aunty should be released immediately as she's being detained unlawfully," the politician said.Proof of lifeAuthorities have not disclosed the exact location of Suu Kyi's detention in the capital Naypyidaw, nor how many years of her sentence remain.Her son, Kim Aris, a British national, has sought independently verified proof of his mother's life after she was transferred to house arrest.He says he has not heard from his mother, who remains massively popular inside Myanmar.Since the coup, Myanmar has been largely ostracised by the international community, and the 11-nation Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) has excluded the country's leadership from high-level summits.But neighbour Thailand has been leading an effort to bring the once pariah state back in the diplomatic fold, both bilaterally and through the regional bloc.Since his change in position, Min Aung Hlaing has travelled to India, China and ASEAN member Laos, and he is scheduled to make an official visit to Thailand this week.Despite the diplomatic outreach, the continued detention of Suu Kyi remains a major sticking point for some nations.The ASEAN bloc has pressed for its special envoy to meet Suu Kyi, but so far Myanmar has refused.Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow told reporters last month that Myanmar's Foreign Minister Tin Maung Swe had assured his regional counterparts during a trip to Thailand that Suu Kyi was "in good health.""We have been told she has been taken care of well but it needs to be proved," Sihasak added.

https://www.theguardian.com/australia-ne.text: The onus will be on social media companies to identify and mitigate risks on their platforms under the government’s proposed legislation, Insiders host David Speers says, and that legislation will be unveiled this week. He says it will cover illegal content including illegal pornography being made available to adults, and for kids there would be “around half a dozen additional areas of psychosocial harm and that includes content around body image and bullying”. He says: The companies would face hefty fines of more than $100m if they fail to restrict this content and as for algorithms – regular pop-up messages would be required, asking if users want to stick with the algorithm or only see people they’re following and see what they’re posting. The user would have the choice. Researchers and the eSafety commissioner would also be empowered to police the social media platforms by using what are called ‘sock puppets’ posing as children to monitor what is being fed to kids online. Sikorski noted that Kaliningrad currently holds “practically no troops” because the Kremlin assumes NATO will not act, suggesting decisive allied maneuvers would inject strategic ambiguity. by Kyiv Post | Sept. 13, 2026, 3:37 pm Flip Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied Poland’s Minister of Foreign Affairs Radoslaw Sikorski takes part in a joint press conference with India’s Minister of Foreign Affairs after their meeting at the ministry building in Warsaw, Sept. 04, 2026. (Photo by Wojtek RADWANSKI / AFP) Content Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied Flip NATO should conduct aggressive military exercises along the borders of Russia’s Kaliningrad exclave to exploit Moscow’s local troop drawdown and compel the Kremlin to divert forces away from Ukraine, Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski said on Friday, Sept. 11. Speaking at the 22nd Annual Meeting of the Yalta European Strategy (YES 2026) in Kyiv, organized by the Victor Pinchuk Foundation, Sikorski stated that Poland monitors the Russian exclave closely and observed that Moscow has left the heavily militarized territory virtually depleted of conventional ground forces to replenish combat losses in Ukraine. JOIN US ON TELEGRAM Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official . “Putin knows, or assumes, that NATO is a peaceful alliance and we will not take advantage of his local weakness. And, perhaps, that is a mistake,” Sikorski told conference participants, as reported by European Pravda . Advertisement Clarifying that he was not advocating for allied forces to seize the Baltic enclave, Sikorski emphasized that NATO should use high-intensity maneuvers to inject strategic unpredictability into Moscow’s defense planning. “I propose that we hold drills on our side so aggressive that he is not sure what exactly we will do,” Sikorski explained. “And so that because of this, he would be forced to redeploy part of his forces from Ukraine.” Heightened border alert Sikorski’s remarks follow warnings from Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk that Moscow may orchestrate provocations and strikes targeting border infrastructure between Ukraine and neighboring allied nations. Other Topics of Interest Territory Remains Main Obstacle to Ukraine-Russia Deal, Kushner Says Jared Kushner said territory is the primary obstacle to a peace deal, as mediators seek a creative formula between Kyiv and Moscow. Speaking in Bratislava on Sept. 10, Tusk announced that Polish security services had cooperated with Ukrainian counterparts overnight to avert a direct threat to a border checkpoint. Tusk noted that Russian forces had already targeted border transit hubs, pointing to a deadly drone strike on the Tudora-Starokozache border crossing between Ukraine and Moldova on Sept. 8-9 that killed two Ukrainian nationals and injured seven others. Tusk stated that he had reviewed intelligence dispatches received directly from the US Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) detailing anticipated Russian escalations in the coming months, urging European allies to reinforce collective defenses across NATO’s eastern flank. Advertisement Concurrently, Poland’s Minister Coordinator of Special Services Tomasz Siemoniak met with CIA Director John Ratcliffe in Washington to assess the threat of Russian hybrid warfare and conventional aggression against alliance members. Ratcliffe’s prior diplomatic discussions in Moscow reportedly included direct warnings cautioning the Kremlin against testing allied commitments in the Baltic region. https://www.politico.eu/article/marine-l.text: Welcome to Declassified, a weekly humor column . The year is 2030 and French President Marine Le Pen’s sweeping overhaul of both her own country and the EU shows no sign of slowing down. The Berlaymont, or the European Commission’s HQ, has been repurposed as the Ministry of National Sovereignty, except for the 13th floor —the current work base and living quarters of Commission President Ursula von der Leyen — which is now a cat cafe. Advertisement Advertisement Other buildings in the EU Quarter of Brussels (or, as it’s now known, the 21st arrondissement ) have not been so lucky. Most have been razed to the ground. Some have been occupied by disgruntled former EU staff, who are refusing to leave and have set up a working group to discuss a future roadmap that will feed into a discussion on how to bring back a European Union that Le Pen has largely destroyed. Largely, but not completely. There is still an official EU office; the corner table in the branch of sandwich shop Exki near the Schuman roundabout (ironically, Le Pen used some of the money saved from dismantling the EU to finish the roundabout as planned). It is staffed 24/7 by Maroš Šefčovič, and he has a plentiful supply of leaflets. Le Pen had more in store for the EU after her crushing 2027 presidential election win over Kylian Mbappé (who won a primary against Raphaël Glucksmann to be the unity centrist candidate, which was decided by who could do the most keepie-uppies). The phrases “non-paper,” “stakeholder” and “trilogue” have been consigned to la poubelle de l’histoire . The European Committee of the Regions and the European Economic and Social Committee were closed down within weeks of Le Pen taking office, which shocked millions of Europeans who had no idea they ever existed. The European Parliament building is still there but is now occupied by a strange breed of zombie-like creatures wandering aimlessly through the corridors in search of something to do. No one can tell the difference. Von der Leyen was, as Le Pen promised would happen, sent back to Germany where — in a somewhat unexpected move — she has become chancellor, succeeding Angela Merkel, who herself came out of retirement and orchestrated a coup to bring down current Chancellor Friedrich Merz. Anyway, back to 2026 and an EU reeling from a Le Pen speech in which she pledged to turn the Commission into a “secretariat” in the service of its member countries, and scrap some institutions altogether. Advertisement Advertisement Le Pen gave her speech in Brussels on Wednesday and caught the train from Paris to Gare du Midi — if you haven’t been, imagine what the train station in Hell would look like, but with paninis. According to POLITICO’s railways correspondent, Miles Trackman, Le Pen was close to running into Michel Barnier, a former French prime minister (and who among us hasn’t been French prime minister?) and fervent Europhile who was spotted at the Paris station at the same time. The question being asked in Brussels circles (and everything in Brussels goes around in circles) is: “Will Le Pen do a Meloni?” — as in, will she soften her stance if elected? The future of the Schuman roundabout may depend on it. CAPTION COMPETITION “This? Just an ordinary car. Definitely not a getaway car. Why would I need to get away? It’s not as if I’m a lame duck whose country is on fire.” Can you do better? Email us at [email protected] or get in touch on X @POLITICOEurope . Here’s the best one from our mailbag — there’s no prize except the gift of laughter, which I think we can all agree is far preferable to cash or booze. “The drinks are on me. The bugs are on you.” by Giovanni Cellini

https://www.ynetnews.com/article/rkenikm.text: No suspects have been arrested in the attacks on European diplomats and an American photojournalist in the West Bank over the weekend, and Israeli police officials are now accusing European diplomatic missions of failing to cooperate with the investigation into Saturday's assault near the Palestinian village of Taybeh, northeast of Ramallah. According to police sources, investigators have sought detailed witness statements and photographic evidence from the European diplomats who were attacked by Jewish rioters while attending an olive harvest. However, the officials claim that the diplomatic missions involved have so far failed to cooperate with those requests. Police said investigators from the West Bank District had contacted Israel's Foreign Ministry to approach the diplomatic missions and arrange the collection of evidence. As of Saturday evening, according to the sources, the missions had not provided the requested cooperation. Investigators are seeking detailed testimony, video and photographic material, access to the vehicles involved in the attack and permission to collect forensic evidence. Police officials said the requests were intended to help identify the attackers, arrest them and ensure that everyone involved is brought to justice. The investigation is continuing, but no arrests have been made in connection with either Saturday's attack on European diplomats in Taybeh or Friday's assault on American photojournalist Heidi Levine, who works for The Washington Post, in the Palestinian village of Abu Falah. Police said their investigators and the Shin Bet domestic security agency were continuing efforts to identify those responsible for the attack on Levine, who underwent surgery on her hand Saturday. Her daughter, Ashley Milner, said one of the fingers on her mother's left hand had been cut so deeply that the bone and tendon were exposed. Levine also suffered a broken rib, fractures in several vertebrae and cuts across her body. According to police sources, West Bank District commander Maj. Gen. Moshe Pinchi is personally overseeing the investigations into the weekend's violence. He has assigned both cases to the district's central investigative unit, which is working alongside the Shin Bet. Additional investigators have been assigned to the cases, and Pinchi has emphasized the importance of intelligence sharing and investigative cooperation between police and the Shin Bet to identify the attackers and bring them to justice. Saturday's assault on the European diplomatic delegation took place during an olive harvest in Taybeh, the last entirely Christian Palestinian village in the West Bank. The delegation included representatives from France, Belgium and Poland, as well as French Mayor Bernard Baudoux of Aulnoye-Aymeries, whose municipality has a sister-city relationship with Taybeh. "They were attacked by seven adult men, ages 20 and older, who apparently did not come from a nearby outpost but from farther away, meaning they had been specifically summoned," one of the diplomats present at the scene told ynet. "They kicked the French mayor, and he was injured." A European diplomat traveling in one of the vehicles described how the delegation was forced to flee when masked settlers approached carrying sticks and metal crowbars. "The residents of Taybeh invited diplomats and peace activists to the olive harvest to protect them. At one point, we heard that settlers were approaching, so we immediately got into the car and started driving. Then I saw masked settlers carrying sticks and metal crowbars running toward us. It was clear they had no good intentions. It was frightening. They hadn't come to pick olives," the diplomat said. "They kicked the French mayor, and after beating him, they shouted 'Viva la France.' They had recognized the French flag," he continued. "They also attacked the Belgian vehicle. When you see something like that, you say to yourself, 'My God, how can something like this happen?'" The diplomat said the delegation had arrived with security personnel and found it particularly troubling that the violence occurred in an area under Israeli control. "We knew settler violence was serious, but when you witness it firsthand, you understand just how terrible it is, especially for the residents who depend on the olive harvest for their livelihoods," he said. Although the reported assault on Baudoux was not captured on camera, footage subsequently showed him on the ground, while photographs documented a shattered window in a vehicle belonging to the Belgian Consulate. The attacks have provoked an international outcry and exposed conflicting responses among senior Israeli officials. Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar, the IDF and Israeli police condemned the violence, while Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office issued an English-language statement questioning whether the available evidence established the full sequence of events and the identity of those responsible. The Prime Minister's Office also noted that the delegation had entered a sensitive area without prior coordination with the IDF and raised concerns about what it described as a coordinated campaign to discredit Israel and Jewish residents of the West Bank during the olive harvest. Members of the European delegation rejected the suggestion that they should have coordinated the visit with the military. "That is a misleading claim," delegation members said. "Taybeh is in Area B, and visits there do not require coordination. Diplomats visit frequently, and the military has never escorted them or required prior coordination." One of the diplomats also criticized Netanyahu's response, saying the prime minister had failed to acknowledge the significance of the attack on a delegation visiting a Christian community. "The mayor's political background is irrelevant to the question of who attacked him. Netanyahu's statement completely ignores the fact that this is a Christian village and that the delegation came from Catholic countries that consider themselves committed to protecting Christians in the West Bank. In Europe, Netanyahu's statement is seen as shocking," the diplomat said. The incident has also prompted warnings of diplomatic consequences for Israel. Belgian Foreign Minister Maxime Prévot said his country would continue pushing for European Union sanctions against those responsible for settler violence and those supporting it. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot demanded that Israeli authorities arrest and prosecute those responsible for the attack and take urgent steps to protect civilians from further violence. Poland's Foreign Ministry also condemned the incident. The assault on Levine the previous day drew sharp criticism from Washington. U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee described the attack on the unarmed photographer as a despicable act of violence and called for a full investigation, arrests and prosecutions. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio also expressed concern over the incidents and called on Israel to take stronger action against settler violence. "We're very disturbed by those images and what we're seeing. We've asked the Israelis and continue to ask them to crack down on that stuff," Rubio told reporters. The violence has renewed attention on the situation in Taybeh, where residents have reported repeated attacks on homes, vehicles and agricultural land. The village, which holds particular religious significance for Christians, has seen families leave amid growing fears over their safety. In July 2025, following an attack in which rioters set fire to a cemetery and desecrated a church, Huckabee visited Taybeh and described the incident as an act of terrorism. Despite the repeated condemnations from Israeli and foreign officials, no suspects had been arrested in either of the two latest attacks as of Sunday morning. Police say they are continuing their efforts to identify those involved and bring them to justice.
